finding: the rotor's single-precision angle on 0.3's dynamic motor is reproduced by the emulation to about one unit in its last place, not bit for bit: where the two reach the steady window a unit apart, the rotation rates by phase, the motor's angle rate and the magnet's phase move by that unit's effect, which at 10 Hz is beyond the declared tolerances
not_on_the_declaration: the declaration's tolerances for these quantities took 7c1's rule, whose emulation resolution came from the tag's scheme, where the emulation reproduces the tag's single-precision angle bit for bit; on the dynamic motor it does not
control: the emulation with its angle set to 0.3's at 4.95 s, against the same with its own: see runs

the_two_unit_cap_rested_on.run: 0.3's A0 on its dynamic rungs at 10 Hz, float32, under XLA's single-thread CPU flags (--xla_cpu_multi_thread_eigen=false intra_op_parallelism_threads=1)
the_two_unit_cap_rested_on.measured_by: the build of PR #77 while it wrote the rule (not recorded then), repeated by the review of PR #77 (its r6) with the same result, and recorded here from that repeat
the_two_unit_cap_rested_on.reading: the cap of two units sat at the largest offset seen, with no margin: a build of the runtime that lands three units off would have failed the 10 Hz test with no physics changed. The cap is no longer a gate. Under the second declaration this run's angle offset moves by 2 units of 3.05e-5 rad at the start against 1 of 6.10e-5 at the end: no change across the window, within its derived bound

the_allowance.status: removed as a gate in the review fixes of PR #77 (the maintainer's option A, 2026-10-31)
the_allowance.what_it_was: each angle-reading gate held to its tolerance plus (start + end) times one unit's measured move, while neither end was more than two units apart: at 10 Hz, where every run sits one unit off at each end, a widening of the declared tolerances by 3 to 20 times, written after the 10 Hz miss was seen (its form in the commit that first ran the comparison, its cap after the controls)
the_allowance.why_not: it counted its mechanism twice (the move was measured for a shift present at both ends; 0.3's own miss was one move, the rule granted two), and planted, it let through an upstream offset of the angle of two units (5.2 phase tolerances), the magnet turned 1e-4 rad in its mount (8.6) and a downstream rate drift of 10 to 29 field-rate tolerances (the review's B1, W1, W2)
the_allowance.replaced_by: a0_dynamic_expected_differences_b.json, which reads every phase against the angle of the same run

at_3hz_on_cis_runners.measured: the review fixes' CI and stress runs (CI 41243712154; stress 41243712136, 20 runners): on 5 of the 20 stress runners, and on CI's default-lane runners, 0.3's A0 at 3 Hz misses the first declaration's body's and field's rotation rates, and the pose's phase by 1.6438e-5 rad (1.41 of its tolerance), the same value on every such runner; on the other 15, and on this machine, it holds them all
at_3hz_on_cis_runners.reading: the finding is not 10 Hz's alone: where a runner's single-precision rounding parts 0.3's angle from the emulation's by a unit before 3 Hz's window, the first declaration's angle-reading gates miss there too. The first round's CI and its 20 stress runs passed 3 Hz on such runners only through the finding's allowance (inference: the allowance was the only difference between the rules). Every gate of the second declaration held on all of them
